title: Order patterns and stability
summary: Use rational cuts in formula order patterns to build many parameter types, and compare dense orders with the bounded equality patterns of stable theory.
abstract: A single comparison in a linear order can distinguish arbitrarily many positions. The order property asks whether one first-order formula can reproduce these finite patterns, even in a language with no order symbol. Compactness turns such patterns into a rationally indexed configuration, and its cuts give continuum many complete descriptions over a countable parameter set. With one object variable this gives more than countably many descriptions over countably many parameters, violating countable stability. Infinite equality structures behave differently: every finite tuple is described by finitely many equality classes and choices of named points, which bounds their types and rules out order patterns. Comparing these examples separates stability from deciding sentences, uniqueness of a countable model, and requiring only finitely many types.
